methodology: Each result launches a fresh excise CLI or external renderer process. No timed render result is cached; PNGs exist only transiently for same-run fidelity comparison. CPU/RSS are OS-reported process figures and may be null on platforms that do not expose them after exit.

regressionGate.note: Baseline snapshot; no gate evaluated against itself.

baselineNote: Committed baseline for scripts/run-reference-performance-bench.sh (#1386/#1387/#1389). macOS dev machine, 2026-09-06, .NET 10.0.11 from the OFFICIAL Microsoft SDK at ~/.dotnet (the Homebrew formula is gone: its runtime linked Apple's zlib rather than the vendored zlib-ng, a real difference in the compression path a PDF writer exercises). CLI codegen 'jit' — the SHIPPED ReadyToRun binary, deliberately not Native AOT, which is ~0.65x on the typical cohort but 1.16x-1.59x SLOWER on the tail fixtures this bench exists to improve. The gate refuses to compare across codegen modes, so re-record before switching. SIX runs per fixture, merged from TWO separately-timed passes rather than one pass of three: the gate takes medians, and a median over six samples spanning different machine conditions is both steadier and more representative. Within-fixture renderMs spread here: median 1.11x, worst 1.66x. NOISY on this machine, treat changes under ~1.4x on them as nothing: fifty-transparency-groups (1.66x), mesh-shading-type7 (1.44x), acc-compensation-cover (1.35x), nested-forms-dct (1.33x), indexed-4bit-33mp-image (1.15x). SPREAD IS A FUNCTION OF MACHINE LOAD, NOT OF THE FIXTURE — a quiet run has every fixture under 1.09x. Absolute ms are machine-specific: a local yardstick for 'did my change make it faster', never a portable threshold. Wall and RSS are reported but not gated (startup and load dominate them; they produced a false 1.57x regression). Regenerate with EXCISE_REFERENCE_PERF_RUNS=3 scripts/run-reference-performance-bench.sh.
